preconditions.description: The number of nodes n is an integer between 2 and 400 inclusive.
Each of the n lines after the first contains exactly two integers representing coordinates (x, y).

preconditions.expression: all(abs(int(x)) <= 1000 and abs(int(y)) <= 1000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()])
len({(int(x), int(y)) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()]}) == n

postconditions.description: If no valid binary root tree exists, stdout is '-1'. Otherwise, stdout is a non-negative real number representing the minimum total arc length, with absolute or relative error ≤ 10^-6.

postconditions.expression: any(stdout.strip() == '-1', all(any(yu > yv for u, v in edges) for edges in possible_edges))
postconditions.description: If stdout is not '-1', there exists at least one valid binary root tree configuration where all arcs are directed from top to bottom (yu > yv for each arc u → v). Here, possible_edges represents all possible valid edge sets forming a binary root tree with the given nodes.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' implies (min_total_length == float(stdout.strip()) for min_total_length in possible_total_lengths)
postconditions.description: If stdout is not '-1', it equals the minimum possible total arc length among all valid binary root tree configurations. Here, possible_total_lengths is the set of total arc lengths for all valid configurations.
